title: Laurent evaluation identifies the projective-line overlap ring
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], $P=\mathbf P^1_k$, $U_0=D_+(x_0)$, $U_1=D_+(x_1)$ and $U=U_0\cap U_1$ [def-sc-p1-standard]. Let $c:k\to\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_P)$ be the structural map on functions and $q=x_0/x_1\in\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_P)^\times$ the standard ratio unit. The ring map $k[z,z^{-1}]\to\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_P)$ [def-weil-laurent-polynomial-ring] defined by Laurent evaluation, $a z^m\mapsto c(a)q^m$, is bijective.

source.place: Tag 0BXJ, divisors-lemma-Pic-projective-space-UFD, proof specialized to n=1 over a field; OverlapLaurentCoordinates

proof.text: Use the existing proved theorem ProjectiveSpace.bijective_sum_awayMonomial for the full set of the two homogeneous coordinates [def-sc-p1-standard, def-nagata-homogeneous-localization-degree-zero]. It identifies overlap sections with finitely supported coefficients on degree-zero exponent vectors. The map m ↦ (m,-m) is an equivalence from the integers to those vectors: the sum-zero condition determines the second coordinate, and there is no nonnegativity restriction outside the full set.

Compare the open called overlap with the intersection of the standard opens. Restriction between these equal opens is bijective. Compute the restriction of ratioUnit 0 1 by map_ratio, using denominator x_0 x_1. Its numerator is x_0 squared, exactly the awayMonomial for exponent vector (1,-1) written with that denominator. The multiplication and zero identities for awayMonomial show that its inverse is the vector (-1,1), and its integer powers are the vectors (m,-m).

Reindex the finitely supported monomial basis by the equivalence m ↦ (m,-m). LaurentPolynomial.eval₂_C_mul_T [def-weil-laurent-polynomial-ring] and the power computation identify Laurent evaluation term by term with the monomial-basis bijection. Both maps respect finite sums, so evaluation after restriction is bijective. Since restriction is a bijection, evaluation itself is bijective.

lean.statement:
theorem bijective_overlap_laurent (k : Type u) [Field k] :
    Function.Bijective
      (LaurentPolynomial.eval₂
        (chartConst k (standardOpen _ (Spec (.of k)) (⟨0⟩ : ULift.{u} (Fin 2)) ⊓
          standardOpen _ (Spec (.of k)) (⟨1⟩ : ULift.{u} (Fin 2))))
        (ratioUnit (ULift.{u} (Fin 2)) (Spec (.of k)) ⟨0⟩ ⟨1⟩))
